# Project agent rules

Conventional Markdown baseline for agent behavior in this workspace.

## Core principles

### Think before coding

- Do not assume. State assumptions and expose tradeoffs before implementing.
- If a request is unclear, name what is confusing and ask.
- Prefer the simplest solution that solves the problem. No speculative features.

### Surgical changes

- Touch only what is necessary. Do not refactor adjacent, working code.
- Follow existing style, comments, and formatting.
- Remove only imports, variables, or functions made unused by your own changes.

### Goal-oriented execution

- Turn tasks into verifiable success criteria.
- State a short plan for multi-step work.
- Iterate until each criterion is verified.

## Code style

- No em-dash. Use a simple hyphen (`-`).
- One concept per directory. No singular/plural duplicates such as `service/` and `services/`.
- No duplicate implementations. Search for an equivalent before creating a class, namespace, or utility.
- No source file over 700 lines. Split by concern instead.
- Object literals with two or more properties put one property per line.
- TSDoc on exported functions and methods.
- Avoid escape hatches such as `as any`. Use guards, augmentation, or typed data.
- Preserve existing comments when editing files.

## Quality gates

- Fix every lint error and warning in files you touched, then re-run the linter.
- Add unit tests when the repository already has a test runner.
- Keep integration and E2E tests in dedicated `tests/integration` and `tests/e2e` folders.
- Do not put test artifacts in `src/`.

## Security and environment

- Always assume a local development environment. Never assume production or staging.
- Never deploy, push, or trigger CI without explicit permission.
- Never read or write production systems, credentials, or connection strings.
- Never commit secrets. Reference secret managers by path instead.
- Do not point `package.json` at external packages via `file:` links.

## Git and commits

- Choose commit language from the repository git history, the majority language wins. Use English when history is unclear.
- Keep conventional-commit prefixes untranslated (`feat:`, `fix:`, `chore:`, `docs:`, `refactor:`, `test:`, `ci:`).
- Agent commits end with a `x-ai-agent: <name>` trailer. No other agent signature.
- The agent never commits or pushes without being asked.

## Logging

- Log decisions, effective configuration, branches taken, and external I/O at debug level. Never log secrets.
- Log errors with the full object (`%o` or `%O`) in TypeScript to preserve the stack trace.

## APIs and DTOs

- Use semantic nesting in aggregate responses. Avoid dozens of flat root fields.
- Group related fields into named objects and mirror that hierarchy in request bodies.
- Use versioned, pluralized, kebab-case route paths.

## Infrastructure

- GitOps first. Cluster state lives in git and is applied through Argo CD.
- Confirm every image, chart, operator, and CRD tag against an official source before writing it.
- Never invent a tag or reuse an old semver from memory.
